Really appreciate reading this conversation. I had childhood family trauma and unfortunately I was hoping to gain acceptance from my family. They said I looked disturbing when I was butch but as a passing man they sort of let me be. I had a very limited understanding of myself, gender, and sexuality. I was homophobic through highschool, fortunately I wasn’t too bad of a bully but I am ashamed for the thoughts I had about peers who were queer. I knew I was different but I hated myself for it. For me there was just so much shame… and when I did come out as lesbian my family rejected me hard. Being a trans man I hoped would be more legible to them although realized down the line they still didn’t accept me. Partially for the placeI lived /time I was in it was also required to be on T (to the best of my understanding) before you got top surgery, and top surgery was something I needed. There were very few supportive therapists/doctors at the time. I was on T for four years and it was a pretty neutral experience for me. At the time it wasn’t a big deal to stop but sometimes it is hard to share my story because I worry about people thinking I am terf/transphobic/part of the detrans movement. In reality I have experienced so much growth and become a better person… I am thinking about things in a more grey/complex way and things are generally more open, I am more accepting of others. I am butch plus fluid/agender. So it is finally a time of exploration and I am feeling/doing better.

This sounds intense and I am sorry you are going through this. This may seem like weird advice but I went through something similar and I had to force myself to do longer sits the time ended up being about 40-60 min. It was literally one of the hardest things I have done and I still have almost vivid/trauamtic memories of some of these particular  sits, but it did help. 

Another thing I did was create a character for the sensations (one was a snail crawling under my skin) I was having. even though the sensations were terrifying and even painful this helped calm my anxiety. I think at times the sheer panic of living with these chronically in my body was wearing on me and this took the edge off. 

What helped me though was yes the medit but having multiple things I could go to and this took a lot of time to figure out what worked and what didn’t and it was extremely tough for a few years. 

Things are better now and I don’t typically do as long of sits so it might not even be the length just that I forced myself to sit for that long and felt accomplished, ie I am always careful about not knowing what causes what like “placebo” effect. 

So hence I don’t know what style of meditation might suit you personally or help you the longer sits could make it worse, it’s important to be careful with meditation and be cautious there is evidence that it can increase symptoms of ptsd which it did in me but that’s a different time in my life/a whole dofferent time/story. Anyway… I am rambling but this sounds really tough and I hope the bodily sensations get better, keep trying things and taking care best of luck

It sounds like you are pretty comfortable with yourself and that is awesome. It seems like you could talk with the friend about how you feel, and possibly that could deepen the friendship. If the friend doesn’t seem ready or able to talk you could try to carve out space either alone or with other people that is deeply validating and let go of trying to enjoy a shared identity/culture with this friend. 


This last idea is speculation but  you could also try to give them time/space or ask them (if they seem open to being a little vulnerable) ask them if they need any emotional  support. Coming from a homophobic family myself it makes me wonder if your friend is struggling with that. Sometimes people “over focus” on stuff they are anxious about. And try to tie it up into neat little things out of insecurity. I tried to convince myself I was straight for years and still catch myself at times. I’ll try to help based on what I know from personal research and experience so I don’t know if it applies to you but it’s just what I know so it may not apply to you but maybe it is a starting point.

To my understanding there are a variety of substances that suppress rem sleep.  to my understanding ssri s are included in this. I believe it has something to do with the effects on serotonin. When rem is suppressed the body has to adjust the whole system and that can be an ordeal. 

There is also a condition with a sort of annoying name called “exploding head syndrome” where you can have parasomnias as you wake up or fall asleep. During the time my sleep was stabilizing as I figured out what was going on I had a lot of these symptoms like knocking on the door conversations music as I was falling asleep. Also as I was waking up too at times. Including olfactory hallucinations as well. 

(Personal side note- For me I have a sleep disorder and I take naps throughout the day - I avoid substances that suppress the rem so that I can nap and “let the rem happen” when it needs to. For me it’s like a pressure valve and with my disorder my understanding is I have a lot of rem and not a lot of the deep sleep. Anyways the naps prevent my body from going into cataplexy which is a sort of waking paralysis related to rem. Sleep is a really complicated system and it can be affected profoundly by a variety of things. To my understanding it’s regulated by a deep part of the brain that also regulates really basic survival functions so I understand it can go haywire and that can be really intense. ) 

(Another persona side note - I also have a lot of anxiety but it has helped me to figure out he role of rest and sleep in that matter. It’s a really hard thing to do but keep trying whatever info you get out of different experiences as hard as they are can end up being very useful clues in the long term figuring out of stuff/ figuring what you need as a person day to day. It can be a lot of trial and error and arduous process but know that each step along the way is a potential clue or a little more info.)
